name: Duloxetine North American SUI
question: Does duloxetine reduce incontinence episodes and improve incontinence-related quality of life versus placebo in North American women with stress urinary incontinence?

design.population: 683 North American women aged 22–84 years with predominant stress urinary incontinence, at least seven episodes weekly, a positive cough stress test and stress pad test, and bladder capacity at least 400 mL.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Purpose; Materials and Methods

verdictNote: Both stated primary outcomes favored duloxetine; adverse-event withdrawal was higher.
takeaway: Duloxetine 40 mg twice daily versus placebo reduced incontinence episode frequency (50% versus 27%) and improved incontinence-related quality of life over 12 weeks in North American women with stress urinary incontinence; adverse-event withdrawal was 24% versus 4%.

reports.label: Primary 12-week report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation and Crossref publication metadata state October 2003 without a day
reports.citation: Dmochowski RR, Miklos JR, Norton PA, Zinner NR, Yalcin I, Bump RC. "Duloxetine versus placebo for the treatment of North American women with stress urinary incontinence." *J Urol.* 2003;170(4 Pt 1):1259-1263. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000080708.87092.cc

results.measure: Percent decrease in weekly incontinence episode frequency after 12 weeks
results.note: The abstract does not provide an effect interval or endpoint-specific analysis denominator.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods; Results

results.measure: Improvement in Incontinence Quality of Life questionnaire score after 12 weeks
results.note: The abstract does not provide an effect interval or endpoint-specific analysis denominator.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods; Results

results.endpoint: At least 50% reduction in incontinence episodes
results.measure: Proportion with 50%–100% reduction in weekly incontinence episode frequency
results.note: Responder counts and analysis denominators are not reported in the abstract.

results.measure: Increase in voiding interval after 12 weeks
results.note: The abstract does not provide an effect interval or endpoint-specific analysis denominator.

harms.label: Discontinuation because of adverse events
harms.note: P<0.001; event counts and safety denominators are not reported in the abstract.

harms.label: Nausea-associated discontinuation and completion

values.exp: 6.4% discontinued because of nausea; 58/78 (74%) with treatment-emergent nausea completed

harms.note: The abstract describes nausea as the most common adverse effect.

delivery.label: Study regimen
delivery.value: A two-week placebo lead-in preceded randomization to duloxetine 40 mg twice daily or placebo for 12 weeks.
